sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The cover and executive summary of a 2004 report of the WHO Regional Director to the fifty-fourth session of the Regional Committee for Africa (AFR/RC54/6), on ways of implementing World Health Assembly and Executive Board resolutions of regional interest. It notes the resolutions concerned and invites the Committee to comment on the proposed implementation strategies.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION

summary.text: Introduces the report, explaining that it is submitted under an earlier Regional Committee resolution and that a work plan will be prepared to monitor implementation. It begins the section on resolution WHA57.1 on surveillance and control of Buruli ulcer.

sections.extract: 1. The Fifty-seventh World Health Assembly and the one-hundred-and-thirteenth session of the Executive Board adopted a number of resolutions of regional interest. The ways and means of implementing the resolutions of interest to the African Region are contained in document AFR/RC54/6 which the Regional Director hereby submits to the fifty- fourth session of the Regional Committee for consideration and guidance, in

summary.text: Describes regional action on Buruli ulcer under WHA57.1, including support for the Global Buruli Ulcer Initiative, awareness-raising, integrating control into health systems and links with leprosy, TB and guinea worm programmes. It also mentions surveillance and support for research into better diagnostic, treatment and control tools.

sections.extract: REQUESTS the Director-General: to continue to provide technical support to the Global Buruli Ulcer Initiative, in order particularly to advance understanding of the disease burden and to improve early access to diagnosis and treatment by general strengthening of health infrastructures. 6. sections.title: WHA57.2: CONTROL OF HUMAN AFRICAN TRYPANOSOMIASIS

summary.text: Sets out regional action on resolution WHA57.2 on human African trypanosomiasis, including national plans for intensified case detection and treatment, epidemic control in Uganda and a monitoring database. It also notes drug research through TDR, a WHO–Aventis partnership and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

summary.text: Describes regional action on resolution WHA57.10 on road safety and health, including launching WHO's world report on preventing road traffic injuries in four countries and promotion of trauma care guidelines and injury prevention training.

summary.text: Describes regional action under resolution WHA57.11 on family and health, including a life-cycle approach to family health, reaching vulnerable family members and the regional Women's Health Strategy. It also mentions work with partners on strategic plans for family and reproductive health.

sections.title: REQUESTS the Director-General: to take action within the framework of the “Three

summary.text: Continues regional action on HIV/AIDS under WHA57.14, including the Three Ones principle, partnerships and resource mobilization, and prevention including condoms and sterile injecting equipment. It covers scaling up prevention of mother-to-child transmission and improving access to medicines and diagnostics through national medicines policies and prequalification. It also covers supply chain assessments, strengthening health systems and reporting to the Regional Committee and the Health Assembly.

sections.title: WHA 57.16: HEALTH PROMOTION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES

summary.text: Describes regional action under resolution WHA57.16 on health promotion and healthy lifestyles, based on the 2001 regional health promotion strategy. It mentions programmes addressing risk factors such as harmful alcohol use and an initiative to improve communication between adolescents, parents and communities.

sections.title: WHA57.17: GLOBAL STRATEGY ON DIET, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND HEALTH

summary.text: Describes regional action under resolution WHA57.17 on the global strategy on diet, physical activity and health, including continued work on undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies across the life cycle. It also covers promoting healthy diets and physical activity with academic, professional and government partners while avoiding conflicts of interest.

sections.title: PART I: Allogeneic transplantation

summary.text: Describes plans under WHA57.18 to collect data on the practice, safety and ethics of allogeneic transplantation of organs, tissues and cells to update WHO guiding principles. It notes the limited availability of such services in the region and plans to disseminate information to support regional cooperation.

summary.text: Defines xenotransplantation and states that the Regional Office will facilitate communication on it by distributing WHO guidance on surveillance of xenogeneic infections.

summary.text: Explains that WHO collaborating centres will collect and share data on allogeneic and xenogeneic transplantation and that WHO will promptly inform Member States of any xenogeneic infectious events and support national capacity on request.

sections.title: WHA57.19: INTERNATIONAL MIGRATION OF HEALTH PERSONNEL: A CHALLENGE FOR HEALTH SYSTEMS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES

summary.text: Describes regional action under resolution WHA57.19 on international migration of health personnel, including information systems to monitor health worker movement, studies of brain drain and work with the International Organization for Migration. It covers strengthening human resources planning and training, approaching financial institutions on policies affecting recruitment, and a proposed code of practice on international recruitment. It also mentions African Union and NEPAD engagement and the strengthening of WHO's human resources for health programme.
